jobs.title: Chief of Staff
jobs.description:
CHIEF OF STAFF 

Location: Austin, TX (Hybrid on-site, with up to 20% travel supporting executive engagements, customer meetings, and strategic initiatives)
Clearance Requirement: U.S. Citizen with the ability to obtain and maintain a DoD security clearance



About NODA

NODA is a veteran-owned, venture-backed technology company that is transforming how unmanned systems collaborate in complex, mission-critical environments. We are developing next-generation solutions that enable the autonomous orchestration of heterogeneous unmanned systems across air, sea, land, and space with vital applications in the defense, intelligence, and commercial sectors.

The Chief of Staff sits at the center of NODA AI's executive function, serving as a force multiplier for the CEO and leadership team. As NODA scales through its next phase of growth, this role is critical to ensuring the company operates with clarity, alignment, and speed across every function.

Joining NODA means working on meaningful technology that pushes the boundaries of autonomy alongside a team that thrives on innovation, rapid iteration, and collaboration.



The Role

We are seeking a Chief of Staff to serve as a trusted partner and operational right hand to NODA AI's CEO and Executive Leadership Team. You will own the connective tissue that keeps the company aligned, informed, and moving at the pace the mission demands, translating strategic intent into operational execution and ensuring the leadership team focuses its time and energy on the highest-priority decisions and opportunities.

Your work will span executive operations, strategic communications, cross-functional programme management, board and investor relations support, and special projects. You will work across every function of the business, from Engineering and Product to Business Development, Finance, and People Operations, with visibility into everything and accountability for ensuring nothing falls through the cracks.

This role is not a coordinator or scheduler seat. It requires someone who can operate at the strategic level alongside the CEO, drive decisions independently, represent the company with external stakeholders, and build the operational infrastructure that scales with the business.



Key Responsibilities

 - Serve as a trusted partner and strategic advisor to the CEO, providing counsel on business decisions, organisational priorities, and leadership challenges

 - Own the CEO's operating rhythm including calendar management, time prioritisation, meeting preparation, and follow-through on commitments and action items

 - Lead preparation for board meetings, investor updates, executive offsites, and all-hands communications, including materials development, narrative alignment, and follow-up

 - Drive cross-functional strategic initiatives from definition through execution, coordinating across Engineering, Product, BD, Finance, People Operations, and other functions on behalf of the CEO

 - Identify and resolve misalignments, blockers, and gaps across the leadership team before they become problems, escalating with clear options and recommendations

 - Design and run the company's operating cadence including leadership syncs, quarterly business reviews, OKR processes, and strategic planning cycles

 - Develop and maintain executive-level communications including internal updates, external briefings, board materials, investor communications, and customer-facing presentations

 - Partner with the executive team on organisational design, headcount planning, and talent strategy as the company scales

 - Build trusted relationships with key external stakeholders including investors, board members, customers, partners, and government officials, representing the CEO when needed

 - Lead or support special projects and strategic initiatives that require cross-functional coordination or direct CEO involvement

 - Maintain strict confidentiality and discretion across all sensitive business, personnel, and strategic matters



Required Qualifications

 - 8+ years of progressive experience in chief of staff, strategy, management consulting, investment banking, business operations, or a directly comparable role supporting senior executive leadership

 - Demonstrated experience operating at the executive level, partnering directly with a CEO, President, or C-suite leader in a high-growth or mission-critical environment

 - Experience in defense, national security, aerospace, or a regulated technical environment, or demonstrated ability to ramp quickly in a complex domain

 - Proven ability to manage cross-functional initiatives, drive decisions, and deliver results without direct authority across a matrixed organisation

 - Exceptional written and verbal communication, including executive-level presentations, board materials, and external stakeholder communications

 - Strong analytical and structured thinking skills, with the ability to synthesise complex information and translate it into clear recommendations and action

 - Experience designing and running executive operating cadences including leadership syncs, OKR processes, and strategic planning cycles

 - High level of integrity, discretion, and professionalism in handling sensitive business, personnel, and strategic information

 - Due to the nature of the position, U.S. citizenship is required due to ITAR regulations, along with the ability to obtain and maintain a DoD security clearance.



Preferred Qualifications

 - Active DoD security clearance, Secret or higher

 - Prior military service or significant experience working with military or government organisations

 - Experience at a venture-backed startup or high-growth technology company, ideally through a Series A to Series C transition

 - Background in management consulting, investment banking, or private equity with exposure to defence, aerospace, or national security sectors

 - Experience supporting board of directors meetings, investor relations, and fundraising processes

 - Familiarity with federal acquisition, government contracting, or defence procurement environments

 - MBA or advanced degree from a leading institution



Skills & Attributes

 - Strategic operator who thinks at the executive level and executes at the detail level, bridging the gap between vision and delivery

 - Trusted advisor with the judgment and discretion to handle sensitive information and navigate complex stakeholder relationships on behalf of the CEO

 - Proactive and anticipatory, identifying what needs to happen before being asked and removing obstacles without needing direction

 - Exceptional communicator across all audiences, from engineers to board members, both written and verbal

 - Calm and composed under pressure, maintaining clarity and effectiveness when priorities shift rapidly and stakes are high

 - Highly organised, managing multiple concurrent initiatives, commitments, and stakeholders without losing track of details or follow-through

 - Collaborative partner who builds trust quickly across functions while maintaining appropriate boundaries and confidentiality

 - Mission driven, with a genuine commitment to NODA AI's defence mission and the people who serve it




BENEFITS & PERKS

Our culture fosters collaboration, respect, and trust, empowering passionate people to do their best work. We offer a competitive salary, comprehensive benefits, and opportunities for career growth. In addition to an opportunity to take part in an innovative, collaborative and fast-growing business with a highly motivated and skilled team, we also take pride in taking care of our employees. Here are just a few ways that we show our appreciation:

 - We offer premium medical, dental, and vision coverage with zero paycheck premiums for you and your family

 - 401(k) Retirement Savings Plan to invest in your long-term retirement goals + Company match

 - Equity grants for new hires

 - Unlimited PTO

 - 11 Paid holidays

 - Extremely generous company holiday calendar, including a holiday hiatus in November, & December.

 - Generous Parental Leave

 - Military Leave for annual training or service requirements

 - FSA

 - DCFSA

 - HSA

 - Professional Development Opportunities

 - Access to One Medical https://www.onemedical.com/

 - Mental Health Resources: We provide free mental health resources 24/7 including therapy and more. Additional work-life services, such as free legal and financial support, are available to you as well.

To conform to U.S. government export control regulations, including the International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR) and Export Administration Regulations (EAR), you must be a U.S. citizen, lawful permanent resident of the U.S., protected individual as defined by 8 U.S.C. 1324b(a)(3), or otherwise eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State or U.S. Department of Commerce.

BUSINESS DEVELOPMENT MANAGER, SPECIAL OPERATIONS – NODA AI

Location: Remote, US (With approximately 30% travel supporting customer engagements, demonstrations, and industry events)
Clearance Requirement: U.S. Citizen with the ability to obtain and maintain a security clearance



About NODA

NODA is a Veteran-owned, venture-backed technology company that is transforming how unmanned systems collaborate in complex, mission-critical environments. We are developing next-generation solutions that enable the autonomous orchestration of heterogeneous unmanned systems across air, sea, land, and space with vital applications in the defense, intelligence, and commercial sectors.

Our Business Development team plays a critical role in shaping how autonomous systems are adopted across the defense enterprise, influencing requirements before they are written, shaping acquisition strategies before they are released, and accelerating the transition of next-generation autonomy capabilities from concept to operational deployment.

Joining NODA means working on meaningful technology that pushes the boundaries of autonomy alongside a team that thrives on innovation, rapid iteration, and collaboration.



The Role

We are seeking a Business Development Manager to lead growth across the U.S. Special Operations community. This is not an account management role. This is a builder's role.

You will identify emerging mission needs, establish trusted relationships across the Special Operations enterprise, influence acquisition strategies, and lead opportunities from initial engagement through contract award. You will work directly with operators, acquisition professionals, Program Executive Offices, prime contractors, and industry partners to position NODA where our technology creates operational advantage.

Success in this role requires initiative, sound judgment, intellectual curiosity, and the ability to operate independently in a fast-moving startup environment where priorities evolve quickly and opportunities are often created rather than assigned. The ideal candidate is equally comfortable discussing operational challenges with end users, technical integration with engineers, and acquisition strategy with senior government leaders.

Preferred Qualifications

 - Experience supporting autonomous systems, AI-enabled software, unmanned systems, ISR, C5ISR, robotics, mission autonomy, or adjacent defense technologies

jobs.title: Export Controls & Trade Compliance Manager
jobs.description:
Export Controls & Trade Compliance Manager

Location: Austin, TX or Washington, D.C. (Hybrid on-site, with up to 5% travel)

Clearance Requirement: U.S. Citizen with the ability to obtain a security clearance



About NODA

NODA is a Veteran-owned, venture-backed technology company that is transforming how unmanned systems collaborate in complex, mission-critical environments. We are developing next-generation solutions that enable the autonomous orchestration of heterogeneous unmanned systems across air, sea, land, and space with vital applications in the defense, intelligence, and commercial sectors.

Our Operations team plays a critical role in ensuring NODA can move quickly, responsibly, and compliantly in a highly regulated defense technology environment. As our products, partnerships, programs, and international activities scale, trade compliance is central to how we develop technology, collaborate with customers and partners, protect controlled information, and execute across the business.

Joining NODA means working on meaningful technology that pushes the boundaries of autonomy alongside a team that thrives on innovation, rapid iteration, and collaboration.



The Role

We are seeking an Export Controls & Trade Compliance Manager to serve as the day-to-day operational owner for NODA AI's export controls and trade compliance activities. You will be responsible for the mechanics that keep our program running: import and export compliance, restricted party screening, licensing administration, jurisdiction and classification, government submissions, training, foreign person and visitor controls, audits, and recordkeeping.

You will work closely with outside export compliance counsel on matters requiring specialized legal or regulatory interpretation and translate that guidance into practical action. You will also partner across Engineering, Business Development, Contracts, the Information System Security Manager (ISSM), Facility Security Officer (FSO), People Operations, and Finance to embed trade compliance into how NODA AI operates rather than treating it as an after-the-fact review.

This role is for someone comfortable operating at the intersection of technology, national security, regulation, and execution. You can move quickly without sacrificing rigor, understand enough about complex technical products to ask the right questions, and bring structure to an environment where requirements and priorities evolve quickly. You know when to independently execute established processes and when a question requires escalation to outside counsel. Most importantly, you are an operator who keeps licenses moving, records audit-ready, employees trained, controlled information protected, and compliance requirements from becoming barriers to execution.



Key Responsibilities

 - Serve as NODA AI's internal subject matter expert and operational owner for export controls and trade compliance, driving program execution, policy implementation, regulatory change management, and cross-functional compliance efforts while partnering with outside counsel on complex legal and regulatory matters.

 - Own and manage DDTC registration and regulatory compliance obligations, including registrations, renewals, required government filings, certifications, reporting activities, and correspondence with the U.S. Department of State, DDTC, BIS, and other applicable government agencies.

 - Prepare, submit, administer, and track export licenses, agreements, authorizations, and classification requests through U.S. Government systems, including DECCS and SNAP-R, covering DSP-5 licenses, TAAs, MLAs, commodity jurisdiction and classification requests, and other applicable export authorizations.

 - Perform, document, and maintain written jurisdiction and classification determinations for software, source code, technical data, hardware, and integrated systems under the USML and CCL/ECCN frameworks, partnering with Engineering and Product to understand functionality, technical characteristics, end use, and changes that may affect existing determinations.

 - Perform and document restricted and denied party screening for customers, partners, vendors, visitors, and foreign persons, and administer foreign person and visitor compliance requirements, including screening, access reviews, DDTC notifications, certifications, deemed export considerations, and supporting documentation.

 - Administer applicable ITAR exemptions, EAR license exceptions, Technology Control Plans, and Technology Transfer Plans, maintaining accurate records of licenses, agreements, classifications, provisos, exceptions, exemptions, expiration dates, reporting requirements, and continuing obligations.

 - Partner with the ISSM, FSO, IT, Security, Engineering, and other stakeholders to control and document access to export-controlled information across company systems, development environments, repositories, facilities, and restricted environments, including reviews of software and technical data releases and technology transfers.

 - Support import and cross-border compliance activities, including tariff classification, country-of-origin and customs documentation, international shipments, demonstrations and deployments, and coordination with customs brokers and freight forwarders.

 - Deliver new-hire, role-specific, and recurring export-control training; conduct internal audits and self-assessments; support internal compliance investigations and potential violation reviews; document findings; track corrective actions through closure; support government inquiries and compliance reviews; and maintain complete, organized, and audit-ready trade compliance records.

 - Maintain and continuously improve NODA AI's Export Management and Compliance Program (EMCP), partnering cross-functionally to address licensing, export restrictions, end-use and end-user requirements, sanctions, foreign person reviews, and other trade compliance obligations.



Required Qualifications

 - 5+ years of hands-on experience supporting or executing U.S. import, export, or trade compliance activities, including practical experience with ITAR and EAR requirements.

 - In-depth working knowledge of ITAR, EAR, OFAC sanctions requirements, the Commerce Control List (CCL), Export Control Classification Numbers (ECCNs), U.S. Munitions List (USML), and deemed export concepts.

 - Hands-on experience preparing, administering, or tracking DDTC and/or BIS export licenses, agreements, authorizations, or classification requests, including DSP-5s, TAAs, MLAs, or similar authorizations.

 - Familiarity with U.S. Government trade compliance systems, including DECCS and SNAP-R.

 - Demonstrated ability to prepare and coordinate regulatory correspondence, notifications, requests, and approvals with DDTC and other applicable U.S. Government agencies.

 - Proficiency in restricted and denied party screening, including maintaining complete and accurate compliance documentation.

 - Familiarity with administering Technology Control Plans, Technology Transfer Plans, and similar export-control access and authorization requirements.

 - Working knowledge of U.S. import and customs compliance requirements.

 - Strong working knowledge of trade compliance recordkeeping in an audit-ready environment.

 - Bachelor's degree in Business Administration, Supply Chain Management, Finance, or a related field.

 - Due to the nature of the position, U.S. citizenship is required due to ITAR regulations, along with the ability to obtain and maintain a DoD security clearance.

Preferred Qualifications

 - Active DoD security clearance, Secret or higher.

 - Graduate degree in Business, Law, Finance, or a related field.

 - Experience in defense technology, aerospace, autonomous systems, robotics, or another highly regulated technical environment.

 - Experience supporting a registered ITAR manufacturer and exporter or U.S. Government contractor.

 - Experience supporting international defense programs, including Foreign Military Sales (FMS), Direct Commercial Sales (DCS), international demonstrations, overseas deployments, or similar cross-border defense activities.

 - Experience with BIS commodity classifications, license applications, and EAR license exceptions.

 - Experience conducting internal trade compliance audits, self-assessments, investigations, voluntary disclosures, and corrective-action tracking.

 - Experience coordinating foreign person access controls and deemed export reviews.

 - Certification such as Certified Export Compliance Professional (CECP), Licensed Customs Broker (LCB), CUSECO, or a comparable trade compliance credential.

Skills & Attributes

 - Execution-focused, taking ownership of the mechanics of compliance and consistently closing the loop on licenses, screenings, classifications, records, training, approvals, and follow-up.

 - Detail-oriented, understanding that small administrative errors can create significant regulatory risk and maintaining a high standard of accuracy.

 - Highly organized, managing multiple licenses, deadlines, classifications, approvals, provisos, screenings, and stakeholders without losing track of details.

 - Exercises sound judgment, independently executing established trade compliance processes, recognizing potential compliance risks, and knowing when to escalate to the VP of Operations or outside counsel.

 - Technically curious and operationally practical, willing to learn how complex hardware, software, autonomous systems, and technical architectures work well enough to support accurate compliance decisions and translate regulatory requirements into processes engineers and operators can follow.



Benefits & Perks

Our culture fosters collaboration, respect, and trust, empowering passionate people to do their best work. We offer a competitive salary, comprehensive benefits, and opportunities for career growth. In addition to an opportunity to take part in an innovative, collaborative and fast-growing business with a highly motivated and skilled team, we also take pride in taking care of our employees.  - Mental Health Resources: We provide free mental health resources 24/7 including therapy and more. Additional work-life services, such as free legal and financial support, are available to you as well.

Growth Path at NODA

 - Senior Trade Compliance Specialist – increased ownership of complex licenses, classifications, audits, international transactions, Technology Control Plans, government submissions, and cross-functional compliance initiatives as NODA's international footprint scales

 - Trade Compliance Manager – lead the broader trade compliance function spanning program ownership, regulatory strategy, and organizational capability as the business grows
